title: Adding fractions: 1/2 + 1/4
subject: math
strengths: Most of the class can convert a half into quarters: a quarter fits inside a half exactly twice, so 1/2 = 2/4.
Once every piece is a quarter, the class adds the tops and keeps the bottom: 2/4 + 1/4 = 3/4.

modelAnswers.question: Write 1/2 as quarters, then use your answer to work out 1/2 + 1/4.
creditPoints: The half must be re-cut into quarters before the pieces can be counted together
Carries the working through to the correct final answer

modelAnswers.question: What is 2/4 + 1/4? Explain in one sentence why the bottom number does not change.
modelAnswers.answer: 3/4. The bottom number stays 4 because the pieces are still quarters - the piece size never changed, so only the tops are added.
creditPoints: When the bottom numbers already match, the pieces are already the same size: add the tops (2 + 1 = 3) and keep the bottom number, which only names the piece size
Carries the working through to the correct final answer

commonErrors.example: On the exit ticket question about 1/2 + 1/4, the wrong answer 2/6 adds 1 + 1 for the tops and 2 + 4 for the bottoms.

fixIt.prompt: Fix it: 1/2 + 1/4 = 2/6. First convert the half into quarters, then add the tops only.

commonErrors.example: On the worksheet, a classmate explains: 1/2 + 1/4 = 2/6, because 1 + 1 = 2 and 2 + 4 = 6.

fixIt.prompt: Fix it: explain in one sentence why the bottom number is never added, then write the correct sum.
fixIt.corrected: The bottom number names the piece size and the pieces stayed quarters: 1/2 + 1/4 = 2/4 + 1/4 = 3/4, not 2/6.

nextSteps: Reteach the piece-size idea with a bar re-cut into quarters before any adding happens.
Practise converting halves to quarters until 1/2 = 2/4 is automatic, then add.
